Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex Lie algebra, and let $T(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{n\ge 0}\mathfrak g^{\otimes n}$ be its tensor algebra. Let $I\subseteq T(\mathfrak g)$ be the two-sided ideal generated by all elements

$$x\otimes y-y\otimes x-[x,y] \qquad (x,y\in \mathfrak g).$$

The **universal enveloping algebra** of $\mathfrak g$ is the quotient algebra

$$U(\mathfrak g):=T(\mathfrak g)/I.$$

The image of $x\in \mathfrak g$ in $U(\mathfrak g)$ is again denoted by $x$. The defining relation is therefore

$$xy-yx=[x,y] \qquad (x,y\in \mathfrak g).$$

This is the quotient algebra used throughout the page for PBW, the Casimir element, and the Harish-Chandra projection.

$$\alpha^\vee:=\frac{2H_\alpha}{\alpha(H_\alpha)} \in \mathfrak h,$$

$$s_\alpha(\lambda):=\lambda-\lambda(\alpha^\vee)\alpha \qquad (\lambda\in \mathfrak h^*).$$

The subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}(\mathfrak h^*)$ generated by these reflections is the **Weyl group** $W$, acting on $\mathfrak h^*$ in the usual way.

Fix a positive root system $\Phi^+$ as in [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]]. The **Weyl vector** for that choice is

$$\rho:=\frac12\sum_{\alpha\in \Phi^+} \alpha \in \mathfrak h^*.$$

This is the shift used in the dot action and in the quadratic Casimir eigenvalue formula on this page.

derivations.claim: If $f$ is dot-invariant, then for every $w\in W$ and $\lambda\in \mathfrak h^*$ one has $$ (Tf)(w\lambda)=f(w\lambda-\rho)=f\bigl(w\cdot(\lambda-\rho)\bigr)=f(\lambda-\rho)=(Tf)(\lambda), $$ because [F1] gives $$ w\cdot(\lambda-\rho)=w\bigl((\lambda-\rho)+\rho\bigr)-\rho=w\lambda-\rho. $$

derivations.claim: By [[thm-harish-chandra-isomorphism-for-the-center]], the center $Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ is isomorphic to the Weyl-invariant polynomial algebra $S(\mathfrak h)^W$.
